desc_en:
Time is really fast. No, too fast.
June flew by so mindlessly that it was one of those months where I even wondered... what did I even do?

First of all.. during finals, I really hated myself.
No matter how I look at it, the way I approached the finals was the exact opposite of the person I had been reminding myself to be, from February, or maybe even earlier.

It's not that I wasn't studying. But the mindset itself was so different from midterms.
I remember saying this to one of my classmates during midterms.
"When are you going to start studying for midterms?" Surprisingly, this was 5 weeks before the exam.
I also said, "I'm going to start now." Surprisingly, this was 4 weeks before the exam.

But during finals, I said this to that same classmate.
"For some reason I'm not nervous?"
"I don't know,, even if I try... it's going to be whatever anyway. haha;;"

During midterms I was so strangely anxious that I studied as if I were being chased by anxiety.
I didn't want to feel that anxiety, so I studied more, focused more, stayed lower, and tried to learn more.
And in the end I collapsed, and even though the other subjects came back with scores I could be satisfied with,
I still don't think I ever praised myself for it.

Instead..
the thought went straight to 'satisfaction -> now that I know how it turns out, for finals I'll... even more'

But when finals actually arrived, I couldn't focus on them.
No, it's not that I couldn't. I didn't.

So the day finals ended, I went straight to the lab.
I brought just one thing. My diary.

In the lab, I compared the version of me from the season of preparing for midterms
with the recent version of me.

It's really pathetic. Even I looked at it and thought, "This person lost their beginner's mind."
It was a version of me with humility and desperation deleted, and in that process I really hated myself.

But no matter how I think about it, this is me evaluating myself,
so I figured my brain would just go nooo you're doing fiiiine ~.~ on its own,
so I went to my advisor.

Of course.. I didn't just barge in from the start like please evaluate me !!!!
The scores for my advisor's class were posted that same day the exam ended,
~~this is another reason I respect my advisor. The exam ended that day,
and that evening he graded it and even entered it into the LMS..;;~~

I checked the score, told him I wanted to look at the exam paper, looked at it,
and before leaving after greeting him in his office, I said this.

"Next time I'll.. work harder. I really, ha.. haha;;"

The professor who heard those words.. smiled.

And maybe he sensed that I was blaming myself,
because I sat down and we talked more.

He told me that overall I was doing fine,
but even now, when I think about that time, I still don't understand myself.
Humility and beginner's mind were things I absolutely had to hold onto, and I lost them.

But what's really strange is...
when I do OCW, or biology, or math...
biology and math are still at the high school level, and in front of those I still
put on every kind of humility;;;

During OCW? I can't even describe it. I want to know everything in the lecture notes,
so I read the notes, take notes, and the moment I go wait?, I look it up right away and try
to understand it by any means.

Of course I still think even this isn't enough.

Looking at my diary from the midterm period, what's really pitiful is
not just my own wishes, but that I looked like someone who invented a delusion that the professor would withdraw the lab offer,
believed it as reality, and ran with meeting the professor's expectations as my main purpose.

Looking at my diary from the finals period, I really.. hahahaha

Aaaaaaaaah okay that's enough self-blame, done done done, I won't blame myself anymore....

That's how June went..
Preparing for finals -> finals -> blame blame blame

So maybe the day the exam ended? Or the next day
I kept throwing this infinite question at myself: how am I going to recover this?
The answer hasn't come out yet.. I'll share it once I have one..

Honestly.. wait, no. Sorry, I said I wouldn't blame myself
The fact that I can break a promise I made with myself this easily
is, on one hand, really scary, and the more puzzling part is: why does the brain do that?

Isn't it so strange?
If you lose humility and beginner's mind, the ending is cortisol secretion — couldn't it have predicted that?
If it can predict it, why did it lead me there? Was there not enough cortisol? That doesn't make sense
I wrote it down in my idea notebook.

From June into early July, I'll probably invest about two weeks
because there's a certification I have to get at school, and after that I plan to study straight through.

First, my goal is to clear the entire high school curriculum this summer vacation,
but it's not easy... I don't know if anyone reading this will know or read or see this, but if it were Just studying math :) Just studying science :)
I'd already be done with time to spare. I might have already started cognitive neuroscience.

But the fact that it's not that is the biggest problem.

If I assume I'm studying math, my workflow looks like this

Learn math concepts and proofs -> organize in Obsidian -> organize on a legal pad as if I'm teaching my younger sibling -
-> implement the concept in Python

This takes quite a bit of time. Math I, Math II, and calculus I can handle to some extent,
but I can't predict how long geometry and probability & statistics will take.

If I assume I'm studying science?
My workflow looks like this.. haha

Learn science concepts -> organize in Obsidian -> organize on a legal pad again

This takes a bit less.
But the problem here I feel like there are no answers, only problems, ah I said I wouldn't blame myself is..
I really like biology and physics. But chemistry. Chem istry. This is... really scary.
It's so confusing, and once it tangles there's no way out.. The thought I have every time I do chemistry?

"These elements you can't even see with your eyes ;;" I'd like to apologize here to people who work in chemistry

Of course I know chemistry is very important in cognitive neuroscience and computational neuroscience,
but... there seems to be a gap between something being important and whether my head can actually take it in...
And of course, after saying all this, once I open a chemistry book I'll bury my face in it again,
and once I'm done I'll clearly start grumbling again.

Ah this is getting too long, let's wrap up !!

June. No, the month of passing-over. No, June
I was so disappointed in myself,
but maybe this too is a meaningful failure, and I want to end the self-blame in the early-to-mid part of this post.

And I want to let June pass over to July like this as well.
Let me straighten my tie a little and find my weight again !

Even if there is a day when not a single white butterfly
comes to a flower garden grown with all my strength,
I hope I have not yet fully bloomed.

For the day I will bloom, I will endure and wait through summer, autumn, and winter,
and on that spring day when warm sunlight shines on me, I want to bloom beautifully, so beautifully.

June..... 2-bye!^{-1} (=> original function: bye-2!)
